{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-p0rc","title":"[review] project-LICHEN-worker6-ldv2: TH_2_input missing C_R connection identifier — RFC 9528 violation","description":"In edhoc.py, both EdhocInitiator.process_message_2() (line 388) and EdhocResponder.prepare_message_2() (line 597) compute TH_2_input without including C_R, the responder connection identifier.

Per RFC 9528 Section 4.1:
TH_2 = H( TH_2_input ) where TH_2_input = [ G_Y, C_R, H(message_1) ]

Current code (initiator):
  th_2_input = cbor2.dumps(g_y) + cbor2.dumps(h_msg1)
Should be:
  th_2_input = cbor2.dumps([g_y, c_r, h_msg1])

Current code (responder):
  th_2_input = cbor2.dumps(self._eph_pk) + cbor2.dumps(h_msg1)
Should be:
  th_2_input = cbor2.dumps([self._eph_pk, self.c_r, h_msg1])

The c_r variable is available (extracted at line 381 for initiator, self.c_r defined at line 591 for responder) but not included. Omitting C_R produces a wrong transcript hash, which cascades into incorrect key derivation (prk_2e, keystream_2, mac_2, th_3, prk_3e2m, etc.) and will cause protocol failure against any standard-compliant EDHOC implementation.

This commit's change (raw byte concat → cbor2.dumps() concat) was a partial fix adding CBOR encoding but missed the missing C_R issue.","status":"open","priority":0,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"agent@lichen-project.dev","created_at":"2026-07-24T19:38:13.464778376Z","created_by":"AI Agent","updated_at":"2026-07-24T19:38:13.464778376Z"}
